artifact_kind: Independent English readback of formal Lean declarations

method.semantic_input: Formal Lean text only, after removing nested block comments and line comments while preserving strings. No informal comments, reference prose, or other readbacks were used.
method.verification: Source inspection only. No Lean elaboration, compilation, CI, API, or Git commands were run.
method.workspace_changes: None. Output is confined to this unique temporary directory.
method.dependency_policy: Only the listed local Definitions files were read for dependency context. Mathlib files and several deeper project dependencies were not opened.
method.immutability: This JSON and its SHA-256 sidecar are written once and made read-only; the containing directory is made read-only. This is filesystem read-only protection, not a claim that a privileged process cannot alter it.

shared_context.universe_convention: Write t for the implicit universe used by T : Genl.HeightTheory. Its precise elaborator-generated universe name is not present in the candidate source. The source separately declares u, v, and w. These levels have no equality constraint in the inspected declaration headers.
shared_context.height_theory: T is an arbitrary value of Genl.HeightTheory. Its Curve, each Pt X, and CBS are types at level t. It supplies predicates Hyperbolic and DivisorFree, degree-cutoff sets ptLE X d and ptEQ X d, real-valued htCan, logDiff, and logCond on each Pt X, a distinguished curve tripod with a proof that it is Hyperbolic, and cbsSet : CBS → Set (Pt tripod). Its cutoff axioms are ptLE X 0 = empty and ptLE X (d+1) = ptLE X d union ptEQ X (d+1). No further arithmetic or geometric interpretation of these fields is a condition in this record.
shared_context.domain_abbreviation: Write S = T.cbsSet K intersection T.ptLE T.tripod d, a set of points of T.tripod. K is a supplied value of the arbitrary type T.CBS; d is a natural number.
shared_context.numeric_operations: Natural numbers used in real formulas are coerced to real numbers. The displayed divisions in real formulas are real division; Real.log and Real.sqrt are total real functions. Divisibility and primality premises concern natural numbers.
shared_context.local_height_data: LocalHeightData.{w} is a data record in Type (w+1), containing an index type ι : Type w, a finite subset bad of ι, natural-valued functions p, hv, and f on ι, a natural deg with 1 ≤ deg, prime p(v), positive hv(v), and positive f(v) for each v in bad, and sum of f(v) over bad indices with p(v)=q at most deg for every natural q. The type does not identify ι with actual places of a number field.

local_height_formulas.height: For L : LocalHeightData, L.height = [sum over v in L.bad of hv(v) * f(v) * log(p(v))] / L.deg.
local_height_formulas.heightEq: L.heightEq(q) restricts the same sum to bad indices with p(v)=q, then divides by L.deg.
local_height_formulas.heightOther: L.heightOther(a,b) restricts the same sum to bad indices with p(v) different from both a and b, then divides by L.deg.

declarations.name: AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyLE
declarations.binders: Implicit α : Type at an arbitrary universe level; explicit f,g : α → real numbers and s : Set α. The source also declares an implicit β : Type*, but β is unused and does not enter this definition.
declarations.english: There exists a real number C such that for every x of α, if x belongs to s, then f(x) ≤ g(x) + C.
quantifier_order: Choose one C for the whole set s.
For every x, and every proof that x belongs to s, the displayed inequality holds.
qualifications: C may depend on f, g, and s. It cannot depend on x.
No positivity, normalization, finiteness, or nonemptiness condition is imposed on C or s.
declarations.notation: The expression f ≲[s] g abbreviates this proposition.

declarations.name: AbcAdaptation.Reference.DiscrepancyEquiv
declarations.binders: Implicit α : Type at an arbitrary universe level; explicit f,g : α → real numbers and s : Set α. The unused source variable β is absent.
declarations.quantifier_expansion: There is a real C_forward such that every x in s satisfies f(x) ≤ g(x)+C_forward, and there is a real C_reverse such that every x in s satisfies g(x) ≤ f(x)+C_reverse.
qualifications: The two existential constants are independent.
The definition does not state exact equality of f and g.
declarations.notation: The expression f ≈[s] g abbreviates this proposition.

declarations.name: AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.Corollary22Inputs
declarations.binders: Explicit T : Genl.HeightTheory, K : T.CBS, and d : natural numbers. The local-height-data universe w and the universe t of T are implicit universe parameters. u and v from the surrounding source are unused here. No AG or TG parameter occurs here.
declarations.context: All restricted point hypotheses below use S. The function h and the two predicate fields are defined on every point of T.tripod, even though most constraints apply only on S.

fields.name: h
fields.english: A function from all points of T.tripod to the real numbers.

fields.name: localData
fields.english: For every point x and every proof hx that x belongs to S, a LocalHeightData.{w} value L = localData(x,hx). This is a dependent function on the membership proof, not local data supplied for points outside S.

fields.name: localData_height
fields.english: For every x and hx with x in S, the total height of localData(x,hx) equals h(x).

fields.name: localData_deg_le
fields.english: For every x and hx with x in S, the natural degree of localData(x,hx) is at most 552960*d. This degree bound is in the natural numbers.

fields.name: htCan_equiv
fields.english: The pointwise function x ↦ (1/6)*h(x) is discrepancy-equivalent to the function x ↦ T.htCan(T.tripod,x) on all of T.cbsSet K.
fields.expanded: There exist independent real constants C_forward and C_reverse such that, for every x in T.cbsSet K, (1/6)*h(x) ≤ T.htCan(T.tripod,x)+C_forward and T.htCan(T.tripod,x) ≤ (1/6)*h(x)+C_reverse.
fields.scope_qualification: This field is not restricted by the degree bound d or by membership in S.

fields.name: northcott
fields.english: For every real number H, the set of points x satisfying both x in S and h(x) ≤ H is finite.
fields.scope_qualification: This is finiteness of each height sublevel set within S, not a finiteness assertion for S itself or for all of T.cbsSet K.

fields.name: heightEq_two_le
fields.english: For every x and hx with x in S, localData(x,hx).heightEq(2) ≤ B.

fields.name: HasCyclicSubgroup
fields.english: An arbitrary predicate on a point x of T.tripod and a natural number ℓ.
fields.scope_qualification: No group, representation, subgroup, or arithmetic meaning is defined for this predicate in the inspected structure.

fields.name: TK
fields.english: A real number TK, with no sign condition.

fields.name: cyclic_bound
fields.english: For every x and hx with x in S, and every natural ℓ, if ℓ is prime, 7 ≤ ℓ, ℓ does not divide L.hv(v) for every v in L.bad, and HasCyclicSubgroup(x,ℓ) holds, then ((ℓ-2)/24)*(h(x)-L.heightEq(2)) ≤ 2*log(ℓ)+TK, where L=localData(x,hx).
fields.arithmetic_qualification: Here ℓ-2 means subtraction after coercion of ℓ to the real numbers, not natural subtraction.
fields.premise_qualification: There is no p(v) exclusion, sqrt bound, or outside-exceptional-core premise in this field.

fields.name: SL2Image
fields.english: An arbitrary predicate on a point x of T.tripod and a natural number ℓ.
fields.scope_qualification: The structure does not define this predicate as equality or containment of an actual matrix-group image.

fields.name: sl2_of
fields.english: For every x and hx with x in S, and every natural ℓ, if ℓ is prime, 5 ≤ ℓ, ℓ does not divide L.hv(v) for every v in L.bad, HasCyclicSubgroup(x,ℓ) does not hold, and there exists v in L.bad with p(v) different from both 2 and ℓ, then SL2Image(x,ℓ) holds, where L=localData(x,hx).
fields.premise_qualification: The prime lower bound is 5, not 7. There is no sqrt bound or outside-exceptional-core premise.

fields.name: excCore
fields.english: A set of all points of T.tripod.

fields.name: excCore_finite
fields.english: The intersection of excCore with S is finite.
fields.scope_qualification: No finiteness condition is imposed on excCore outside S, and no proper-subset or nonemptiness condition is imposed on its complement.

declarations.name: AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.ThetaDataExistence
declarations.kind: A proposition-valued structure with one field
declarations.binders: Implicit T : Genl.HeightTheory, AG : AnabelianGeometry.{u}, and TG : TemperedGeometry AG; explicit P : Corollary312VariantData.{u,v} AG TG → Prop; implicit K : T.CBS and d : natural numbers; explicit I : Corollary22Inputs T K d, whose local data use universe w. The height-theory universe t is independent of u, v, and w.

fields.name: thetaData
fields.english: For every point x and proof hx that x belongs to S, if x is not in I.excCore, then for every natural ℓ satisfying the listed premises, there exist X and inv satisfying all listed conclusions.
ordered_binders_and_premises: For every hx proving x in S.
Assume x is not in I.excCore.
For every v in L.bad, assume ℓ does not divide L.hv(v), where L=I.localData(x,hx).
For every v in L.bad, assume that if L.p(v)=ℓ, then the real coercion of L.hv(v) is strictly less than sqrt(I.h(x)).
Assume there exists v in L.bad with L.p(v) different from both 2 and ℓ.
existential_binders: There exists X : Corollary312VariantData.{u,v} AG TG.
quantifier_qualifications: All conclusions hold for the same existential X and the same inv.
The witnesses may depend on x, hx, ℓ, and the supplied premise proofs. No single X or inv is required to work for all x or ℓ.
The sqrt premise concerns only bad indices whose p equals ℓ; the nondivisibility premise concerns every bad index.
The existence of an index with p different from 2 and ℓ is a separate premise.
HasCyclicSubgroup and its negation do not occur as premises of thetaData. SL2Image is required directly.
There is no premise that I.h(x) exceeds I.threshold or any other threshold.

P_coverage.status: P is an arbitrary explicit parameter of the structure, and P(X) is one required conjunct for each witness.
P_coverage.scope: For each fixed P, the proposition ThetaDataExistence(P,I) requires witnesses satisfying that P for every point/prime combination meeting every premise. The declaration is parameterized by P; it does not supply a proof of ThetaDataExistence for every P.
limitations: There is no definition or theorem here establishing P(X), ThetaDataExistence(P,I), or existence of an I.
P need not equal Corollary312Variant and need not imply its inequality. That separately defined proposition is not used in thetaData.
P only takes X as its argument, not inv, x, or ℓ as separate arguments.
If P is constantly false and there is a point/prime combination satisfying every premise, ThetaDataExistence(P,I) cannot hold. If no such combination exists, its single field is vacuous.

declarations.name: AbcAdaptation.Reference.Iut.Corollary22Inputs.threshold
declarations.binders: Implicit T : Genl.HeightTheory, K : T.CBS, and d : natural numbers; explicit I : Corollary22Inputs T K d and cheb : ChebyshevBound. The height-theory universe t and the local-data universe w occur through I. AG, TG, P, u, and v do not occur.
declarations.english: Let δ=552960*d as a real number. Return the maximum of the following four real numbers, grouped as the displayed pairwise maxima.
declarations.formula: max(max(ξ^2, 49 + 8*max(TK,0) + B), max((B + 11 + 2*δ)^4 + 1, ((60*δ)^2*(2*δ + 4))^4 + 1)), where ξ=cheb.ξ, TK=I.TK, B=I.B, and δ=552960*(d coerced to real numbers).
declarations.dependency_qualification: Only cheb.ξ, I.TK, I.B, and d occur in the formula. It uses neither epsilonE nor any point, prime, P, theta witness, height function, or proof field.
declarations.assertion_qualification: This definition alone states no theorem about what happens above the returned threshold.

witness_and_bound_context.ChebyshevBound: A record containing ξ : real numbers, a proof 5 ≤ ξ, and for every real x with ξ ≤ x both (2/3)*x ≤ Chebyshev.theta(x) and Chebyshev.theta(x) ≤ 2*x. The candidate threshold uses only ξ; the definition of Chebyshev.theta in Mathlib was not opened.
witness_and_bound_context.AG_TG: AG is supplied data of type AnabelianGeometry.{u}, a structure in Type (u+1) with abstract orbicurve, cover, base-change, fundamental-group, cusp, Tate-structure, quotient, and geometric-predicate operations. TG : TemperedGeometry AG, also in Type (u+1), supplies tempered-group, topology, comparison, theta-root-model, and canonical-cusp operations. The candidate existence proposition is conditional on these supplied structures, not tied by its header to a uniquely defined concrete geometry.
witness_and_bound_context.Corollary312VariantData: X is data in Type(max(u+1,v+1)) with three fields: data : InitialThetaData AG TG; qPilot : QPilotData X.data; rhsData : RHSData.{u,v} X.data. InitialThetaData contains a number field F, an algebraic closure Fbar, an elliptic Weierstrass curve E, bad-place data, initial global/prime/Tate/orbicurve/local data, and their structure conditions. The inspected global-data definition includes a square root of -1, stable reduction at every finite place, rational six-torsion, a nonempty bad-place set of odd residue characteristic, and multiplicative reduction over it. Further nested dependency definitions were not fully expanded.
witness_and_bound_context.X_ell: X.ℓ abbreviates X.data.ℓ, which is the natural ℓ field of X.data.prime.
witness_and_bound_context.X_dmod: X.dmod is the natural dimension over the rationals of fieldOfModuli(X.data.F,X.data.E). The inspected definition of fieldOfModuli is the intermediate field generated over the rationals by the j-invariant of E.
witness_and_bound_context.X_qPilot_logQ: QPilotData contains a finite set of finite places of F, identified with places over the supplied bad-place set, and a real weight positive on that finite set. X.qPilot.logQ is the sum over those places of weight(w) times the real coercion of the supplied qOrder(w) times log(residueChar(w)). qOrder and residueChar were not unfolded to their deepest definitions.
witness_and_bound_context.Theorem110Invariants: For a fixed X this is a Type-valued data structure explicitly declared as Type. It supplies natural emod with 1 ≤ emod ≤ X.dmod, real nonnegative logDtpd and logFtpd, a finite subset dst of natural prime numbers, and a real-valued logDK on natural numbers that is nonnegative and vanishes outside dst. These are supplied numerical data constrained by this record; their names alone do not identify them with external mathematical invariants.
witness_and_bound_context.Theorem110Certificate: This proposition requires 7 ≤ X.ℓ; residueChar(w) in inv.dst for every w in X.qPilot.badFinset; inv.logDKtot ≤ inv.logDtpd + inv.logFtpd + 2*log(X.ℓ) + 21; and inv.logSQ ≤ 2*X.dmod*(inv.logDtpd+inv.logFtpd) + 5 + log(X.ℓ). Here logDKtot is the sum of logDK(p) over dst, and logSQ is the sum of log(p) over dst.
witness_and_bound_context.LocalEstimate: inv.LocalEstimate is a Type(max(u,v)) data record. Nonempty asserts existence of a value of this type, not merely a numeric inequality and not a chosen estimate field in ThetaDataExistence itself. Its seven fields supply container sets cont(i,vQ), membership of each set in the corresponding hull-region collection, containment of each theta-pilot region, equality to the integral region at finite primes outside dst, a finite-place volume upper bound by capsuleBound at primes in dst, an infinite-place upper bound by capsule cardinality times log(pi), and monotonicity of packet volume for inclusions between hull regions.
witness_and_bound_context.capsuleBound: For natural n,p, capsuleBound(n,p)=n*logDK(p)-((n coerced to real numbers)-1)^2/(2*X.ℓ)*X.logQAt(p)+log(p)+4*n*lmod*ι(p). Here eStar=552960*emod, lmod=log(eStar*X.ℓ), ι(p)=1 when p ≤ eStar*X.ℓ and 0 otherwise, and logQAt(p) is the qPilot logQ sum restricted to residue characteristic p. The nested packet, hull, volume, procession, and RHSData definitions are retained as typed formal context rather than interpreted from their names.

edge_cases_and_logical_limits: DiscrepancyLE and DiscrepancyEquiv are true on the empty set for arbitrary f and g. They impose no pointwise condition outside s.
The discrepancy constants in htCan_equiv can depend on the input record, T, K, and d through its fields, but each is uniform over all points of T.cbsSet K. Neither is a point-dependent error term.

The supplied height theory forces S to be empty when d=0. Consequently local-data constraints, northcott, cyclic_bound, sl2_of, excCore_finite, and thetaData then have no point in S to test; htCan_equiv is still required on all of T.cbsSet K, and B_nonneg is still required.
If S is finite, excCore may contain all of S, making thetaData vacuous on S; in general excCore can contain all of S only if its required restricted finiteness holds.
Even outside excCore, thetaData is vacuous at any ℓ failing any premise. It does not assert the existence of an eligible prime, SL2Image, or an index with p different from 2 and ℓ.

If L.bad is empty, the universal nondivisibility and sqrt premises are vacuous, but the existential p-exclusion premise is false, so thetaData and sl2_of yield no conclusion for that L through these implications.

If no bad index has p(v)=ℓ, the sqrt premise is vacuous. If such an index exists, its hv is at least 1, and the strict sqrt condition forces sqrt(h(x)) greater than 1. The source does not state a separate positivity premise for h(x).
No positive-degree hypothesis on d appears in either structure header. A realized theta witness forces 1 ≤ X.dmod through inv.emod and hence 1 ≤ d through X.dmod ≤ d.
B is constrained to be nonnegative; TK is allowed to be negative and is replaced by max(TK,0) only in the threshold term. The cyclic inequality itself uses TK without truncation.
At d=0, δ=0 and the threshold is max(max(ξ^2,49+8*max(TK,0)+B),max((B+11)^4+1,1)). No singular division occurs in the threshold formula.
LocalHeightData guarantees deg at least 1, so its real height denominators are nonzero. The formulas still use total real division.

No theorem or producer constructs any of the two structures here. No target discrepancy theorem, prime-selection result, Corollary312Variant inequality, or final height inequality is proved by these declarations alone.
